title: Hold My Ring: a party game where 4 players fart to steer one inflatable ring. How AI helped and what I had to throw away
author: 89leon
selftext:
The game is Hold My Ring, a 1-4 player couch/online party game where everyone shares one inflatable ring and farts to steer. The clip is real in-engine gameplay (hockey mode).

How AI was used: I write the code (three.js, rollback netcode, a CPU autopilot that now finishes all 224 level/crew/seat combinations) with an AI coding assistant. The fart SFX and announcer voices are ElevenLabs. Several character models and portraits started as AI generations that I then edited. Nothing is generated while you play.

What didn't work: AI video invented extra people unless the start frame already had them, and generated images sneaked in fake text and logos, so every still gets checked by eye.

What I still do by hand: level design, physics tuning, picking every sound (I listened to a big batch and kept 13), and the final edit.

Not out yet. Questions welcome, especially from anyone who shipped an AI-assisted game and dealt with player reactions.
